title: Tool for Automatically Detecting Benchmark Saturation in Safety Eval Leaderboards
original_idea: Build a Python script that scrapes or ingests benchmark leaderboard data, computes score distributions over time, and flags benchmarks where score variance has dropped below a threshold.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful tool but mostly automates what gen-0661 does manually. The tool itself is less impactful than the analysis it enables.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Python scripting, data scraping, basic statistics. Standard CS skills. No ML or GPU needed. Accessible for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Build a script with clear inputs (leaderboard data) and outputs (saturation flags). Well-defined engineering task. Feasible in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: 'When AI Benchmarks Plateau: A Systematic Study of Benchmark Saturation' (arXiv:2602.16763, 2026) directly and comprehensively addresses benchmark saturation detection with statistical methods including coefficient of variation tracking, slope analysis, and variance thresholds. Brenndoerfer (2025) provides interactive analysis of benchmark saturation metrics and ceiling effects. The GLUE/MMLU saturation trajectories are well-documented. The proposed Python script for scraping leaderboard data and flagging benchmarks where score variance drops below a threshold is essentially a reimplementation of methods already published in arXiv:2602.16763. The engineering contribution (a tool vs. a paper) adds marginal practical value but the analytical methodology is already solved.
